analysis.title: Higher inflation need not derail US assets (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: US equities fell Wednesday after September inflation came in above expectations, raising expectations for further Fed rate hikes. Headline inflation was +0.6% m/m vs +0.4% in August, driven largely by a 9.1% rise in gasoline prices.

Core inflation rose 0.3% m/m, above the 0.2% consensus forecast for a second consecutive month. The annual core rate rose to 2.6% from 2.4%. Price increases also extended to shelter, airfares, vehicles, apparel and technology-related goods.

Markets raised the probability of an October Fed hike to about 40% from about 20% before the release. UBS now expects Fed hikes in December and March, following the September move, then a hold until late 2027.

UBS raised its end-December 10-year Treasury yield forecast to 4.9% from 4.6%. This is below Wednesday's close of 5.19%, and UBS does not expect the revised outlook to undermine its positive view of US assets.

Economic strength is cited as supportive for equities. US GDP growth was close to 2.5% annualized in the first half and likely near 3% in Q3. September payrolls slowed to 29,000, but the three-month average of 51,000 is broadly in line with the pace needed to keep unemployment stable. Initial claims hit a 10-week low and ISM manufacturing was 54.5 in September.

Markets price roughly 3.5 further hikes in addition to September's, versus UBS's expectation of two more. NY Fed President Williams said there is 'no need for urgency', though back-to-back hot core readings make October a closer call. UBS sees scope for yields to fall if the Fed waits in October and inflation pressures stabilize.

UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% for the September quarter, supported by AI demand, cyclical improvement and resilient consumer spending. AI-related capex is expected to rise 84% this year to USD 900bn, and semiconductor profits are expected to account for about half of Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth.

ISM manufacturing new orders have been in expansion for nine consecutive months, supporting the industrial profit outlook. Across 16 Fed hiking cycles since 1954, the S&P 500 gained an average 10.8% in the year after the first hike.

UBS stays positioned for further equity gains with broad diversification across sectors and regions, favors a mix of cyclical and secular equity exposure, and sees value in quality fixed income given higher starting yields.

Germany plans to press the EU to consider safeguards on Chinese chemicals, mechanical engineering and potentially pharmaceuticals (Bloomberg). This follows a record USD 34.8bn Chinese goods trade surplus with the EU in September, almost 21% higher y/y, with exports above USD 60bn for the first time. The EU agreed to cap Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports at 350,000 units a year, potentially from 1 December.

UBS says broader EU trade defenses could create near-term volatility and greater dispersion, but are not a reason to retreat from risk assets. It favors companies with strong balance sheets, pricing power and diversified supply chains, capital preservation strategies, and broad commodities for diversification.

TSMC reported Q3 net profit of TWD 763.1bn, up 68.7% y/y, its sixth consecutive record quarter. It said December-quarter revenue could rise as much as 61% y/y on AI chip demand. This followed ASML's earnings beat and upbeat outlook, though chip stocks have been under pressure on concerns over AI revenue growth.

UBS favors diversified exposure across the AI value chain, emphasizing high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries, megacap platforms and defensive technology companies. Within Asia tech it likes AI chip foundries and the CPU supply chain.

sector_views.rationale: Demand for compute and infrastructure remains robust and cloud growth should accelerate. Favors high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries, megacap platforms and defensive technology.
ISM manufacturing new orders have expanded for nine consecutive months, supporting industrial profits. UBS favors a combination of cyclical and secular equity exposure.
Broad commodities can add diversification against inflation, supply disruptions and geopolitical stress.

TSMC reported Q3 net profit of TWD 763.1bn, up 68.7% y/y (reported, Thursday), the sixth consecutive record quarter. Company said December-quarter revenue could rise as much as 61% y/y (company guidance).
ASML's earnings beat and upbeat outlook preceded TSMC's results (no figures given).

tension_points.bull_case: Strong growth (GDP near 3% in Q3), a resilient labor market and 28% Q3 EPS growth let equities absorb moderately higher rates. The S&P 500 averaged +10.8% in the year after the first hike across 16 cycles since 1954.
tension_points.bear_case: Broad-based core inflation, two straight 0.3% core prints above consensus and market pricing of about 3.5 more hikes could push yields higher. The 10-year closed at 5.19%, and an October hike is about 40% priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed that raises rates more than UBS's two further hikes, or inflation that fails to stabilize after an October pause, would undermine the view that yields decline toward 4.9%.

theme_stances.key_argument: Economic strength driving Fed hikes also supports equities, so moderately higher rates should be absorbed.
theme_stances.evidence: Higher inflation need not derail US assets
